references.text: Describes the firstfruits offering that was to be brought to the Lord, including regulations on when and how the firstfruits of the grain were to be offered.
Mentions the firstfruits of the harvest that are to be brought to the house of the Lord, a parallel to the firstfruits offering in Leviticus.
The command to bring the first of the firstfruits to the house of the Lord.
Refers to the firstfruits of oil, wine, and grain given to the Lord and belonging to the priests.
The ritual for bringing the firstfruits of the land to the sanctuary of the Lord.
Mentions that the Israelites ate from the produce of the land, roasted grain, and fresh ears, which are connected with the firstfruits offering.
A man brought bread made from new grain as a firstfruits offering to Elisha, reflecting the practice of firstfruits offerings.
Complementary instructions on the firstfruits: Lev 2 describes the temple ritual, while Num 15 extends the principle to the home and the dough.
Liturgical context: Lev 23:18 places the firstfruits offering (from Lev 2:14) within the total sacrifice program of the Feast of Weeks.
Direct liturgical connection: Num 28:26 establishes that the firstfruits offering (Lev 2:14) is a central part of the Feast of Weeks.
